claims.claim: ⚠️ **Record consent in the medical record before transfusion**, and follow hospital transfusion procedures.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Blood product prescription' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Blood_product_prescription/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Give a transfusion only when the expected benefit is likely to outweigh the potential hazards.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Blood product prescription' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Blood_product_prescription/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hb under 70 g/L: red cells are often indicated.** A lower threshold can be acceptable when there are no clinical features (tachycardia, flow murmur, lethargy, dizziness, breathlessness, cardiac failure) and specific therapy such as iron is available.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Blood product prescription' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Blood_product_prescription/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hb 70–90 g/L: may be indicated depending on the setting** — bleeding or haemolysis, symptoms and signs of anaemia, or uncorrected congenital heart disease.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Blood product prescription' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Blood_product_prescription/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hb over 90 g/L: often unnecessary and may be inappropriate**, except in particular settings such as haemoglobinopathies (thalassaemia, sickle cell disease) or a congenital anaemia managed on a chronic transfusion program.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Blood product prescription' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Blood_product_prescription/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Volume, under 20 kg:** mL = weight (kg) × 0.5 × desired Hb rise (g/L), prescribed in mL; **maximum Hb increment 20 g/L.** Example: 10 kg child from 60 to 80 g/L = 100 mL. **Over 20 kg: 1 unit, then reassess.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Blood product prescription' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Blood_product_prescription/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Rate: 5 mL/kg/hr**, usual maximum about 150 mL/hr; consider starting at half the prescribed rate for the first 15 minutes.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Blood product prescription' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Blood_product_prescription/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Prophylactic platelets are not indicated for immune-mediated thrombocytopenia** (ITP, HIT, TTP/HUS); congenital thrombocytopenia is an individualised decision.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Blood product prescription' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Blood_product_prescription/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No pre-procedure platelets are needed for bone marrow aspirate or trephine, or for peripheral IV insertion.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Blood product prescription' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Blood_product_prescription/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Volume: under 15 kg, 10 mL/kg (prescribed in mL); over 15 kg, 1 unit.** Rate 10–20 mL/kg/hr — faster transfusion (e.g. over 30 minutes) may cause a reaction.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Blood product prescription' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Blood_product_prescription/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Severe bleeding = any of:** organ dysfunction within 24 hours · haemodynamic instability (HR up or BP down by more than 20% from baseline) · Hb drop over 20% in 24 hours · measurable loss ≥5 mL/kg/hr for ≥1 hour · intraspinal bleeding with neurological loss · intra-articular bleeding limiting movement · intraocular bleeding impairing vision.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Blood product prescription' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Blood_product_prescription/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Moderate bleeding = all of:** more than minimal but not severe · no organ dysfunction · no haemodynamic instability · Hb drop ≤20% · measurable loss ≥1 but <5 mL/kg/hr.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Blood product prescription' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Blood_product_prescription/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **FFP is appropriate for:** acute bleeding with significant coagulopathy · warfarin reversal with significant or life-threatening bleeding (with vitamin K and prothrombinex) · liver disease with significant bleeding and coagulopathy · acute DIC with bleeding · massive haemorrhage · bleeding during or after cardiac bypass · plasma exchange for TTP · factor deficiencies with no concentrate available.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Blood product prescription' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Blood_product_prescription/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **FFP is not indicated** to correct minor INR/APTT prolongation in a non-bleeding child, for minor abnormalities in liver disease without bleeding, or to reverse an INR under 2.0 for minor procedures.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Blood product prescription' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Blood_product_prescription/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **FFP dose: 10–20 mL/kg for all children, at 10–20 mL/kg/hr.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Blood product prescription' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Blood_product_prescription/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cryoprecipitate when fibrinogen is under 1.5 g/L** with active bleeding, in massive haemorrhage (or hyperfibrinolysis), or bleeding during or after cardiac bypass.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Blood product prescription' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Blood_product_prescription/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cryoprecipitate when fibrinogen is under 1.0 g/L** with acquired deficiency or acute DIC and significant bleeding, or before an invasive procedure with significant bleeding risk or at a critical site (neurosurgery, eye surgery).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Blood product prescription' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Blood_product_prescription/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Not indicated** when a child is not bleeding and fibrinogen is only mildly low, or liver disease with minor abnormalities and no active bleeding.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Blood product prescription' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Blood_product_prescription/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cryoprecipitate dose: 5–10 mL/kg for all children, at 10–20 mL/kg/hr.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Blood product prescription' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Blood_product_prescription/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Critical bleeding: transfuse as rapidly as the clinical situation requires.** **Every transfusion must finish within four hours** after the product leaves blood bank.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Blood product prescription' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Blood_product_prescription/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Maximum prescribed volume should not exceed the equivalent adult transfusion.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Blood product prescription' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Blood_product_prescription/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Irradiated products** for all immunocompromised children (every immunology and oncology patient included), neonates who are preterm, low birth weight or have cardiac disease, HLA-matched products and directed donations — the aim is preventing transfusion-associated graft-versus-host disease.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Blood product prescription' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Blood_product_prescription/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **CMV-negative products only** for neonatal exchange transfusion, pregnant women, neonates until 28 days post-term, and CMV-negative children with SCID. At RCH, leucocyte-depleted products are an acceptable alternative.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Blood product prescription' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Blood_product_prescription/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Phenotype-matched red cells** for chronically transfused children or red cell alloantibodies; **IgA-deficient products** for IgA deficiency with anti-IgA antibody; **HLA-matched platelets** for HLA-antibody refractoriness.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Blood product prescription' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Blood_product_prescription/, retrieved 2026-09-23
